claim: Typical people use at least twelve body-networked computers.
originalWording: Typical people use at least twelve body-networked computers.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 5, printed pp. 14–15

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Typical users have at least twelve separately functional worn/carried computing devices linked in a body network.
reference.rationale: Contemporary device-ownership surveys show a handful of gadgets, not typical twelve-node body networks. Phones, watches and earbuds create useful small networks, but not typical twelve-device ensembles. This is a medium-confidence prevalence judgment, not a claim that no enthusiast has twelve devices.

evidence.title: Pew: Americans and their gadgets
evidence.note: US survey, seven broad device categories; median three categories. A proxy for device ownership, not a direct census of worn processors or 2009 body networks..
